extracted.intended_audience: Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) applicants and Licensees; SBA staff and regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and operational standards (Part 107) governing SBIC licensing, financing, operations, reporting, and related activities under the Small Business Investment Act. Covers definitions, licensing procedures, investment limits, financing terms, management consulting rules, and control/transfer rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Part 107
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations in Part 107 implement the functions, powers, and duties conferred on SBA by the Small Business Investment Act of 1958, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all SBA actions and SBIC Licensees under the Act; this section orients readers to the regulatory authority and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information, forms, and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: All SBA forms and instructions referred to throughout Part 107 have been filed with the Office of the Federal Register; copies obtainable from SBA. All applications, reports, or other forms filed with SBA must be completed in accordance with applicable instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified SBA forms and follow the accompanying instructions exactly; appendices contain sample instructions (Forms 468 and 684 referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Associate of a Licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Associate of a Licensee’ includes officers, directors, general managers, investment advisers, attorneys serving the Licensee; persons owning or controlling 10%+ of any class of stock; officers/directors/employees of such persons; persons controlling or controlled by Licensee or such persons; close relatives; concerns in which such persons hold office or own/control 10%+ equity; and persons who held such positions within 6 months before or after financing date are deemed associates as of financing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broad definition governs related-party rules, conflicts, and applicable restrictions; the 6-month look-back/look-forward rule is significant for determining associate status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Close relative
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Close relative’ means ancestor, lineal descendant, brother or sister and their lineal descendants, father-in-law, mother-in-law, spouse, son-in-law, daughter-in-law, brother-in-law, or sister-in-law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the associate definition and other conflict-of-interest provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Control
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Control’ means possession, direct or indirect, of the power to direct or cause the direction of management and policies of a Licensee or small business concern, whether through voting securities, contract, or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines when transfers or changes require SBA approval and when affiliated status exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Debtor Licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Debtor Licensee’ means a Licensee indebted to SBA, including SBA guaranties and commitments with respect thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in provisions applying to Licensees that have outstanding obligations to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Institutional Lender/Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Means banks, insurance companies, and other concerns whose regular course of business entails making commercial and industrial loans or investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes institutional lenders from SBIC financing activities and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Investment Adviser
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who, pursuant to written contract, regularly furnishes advice to a Licensee regarding acquisition, servicing, or disposition of portfolio securities or securities acquired in liquidation; §107.809 governs employment of an Investment Adviser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment of advisers must comply with §107.809; adviser relationships fall under associate/conflict rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — License
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of authority, evidenced by a certificate issued by SBA under section 301 of the Act, authorizing a company to operate solely as a Federal Licensee under the Act and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License conditions, display, and nontransferability rules apply to entities holding this certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: A corporation chartered under State law and granted a license by SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All operational and compliance requirements apply to entities defined as Licensees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Person
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a natural person or legal entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard statutory definition used throughout the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: Securities representing a Licensee’s total outstanding financing of small business concerns; excludes Idle Funds and assets acquired in liquidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to calculate concentration limits, venture-capital ratios, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Portfolio concern
rubrics_metrics.description: A small business concern financed by a Licensee in exchange for debt or equity securities that are still outstanding and constitute part of Licensee’s Portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolio concerns are subject to size-status and nondiscrimination certifications and are counted for investment limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Real estate investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Financing of a small business concern classified as a real estate concern under Major Group 65 of the SIC Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines applicability of certain restrictions and interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 1940 Act Company
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May affect regulatory treatment or exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: The Small Business Administration, with address specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the administering agency for Part 107.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Small business concern
rubrics_metrics.description: A concern (including affiliates per §121.3-2) that meets size standards and criteria in §121.3-11 of Part 121 for size eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees must determine and document size status before financing (see §107.301(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Venture Capital (types of financings considered venture capital)
rubrics_metrics.description: Venture capital includes: (1) Common and Preferred Stock with no repurchase requirement for 5 years (unless SBA approves for relinquishing control); (2) any right to purchase such stock; (3) debentures or loans (convertible or with stock purchase rights) carrying an effective interest rate not to exceed 10%, subordinated to all borrowings from institutional lenders, and with no part amortized during the first 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial for qualifying for SBA funds under §303(b)(2) and for applying the 65% venture-capital ratio in §107.202.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement — management (§107.101(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall have and maintain qualified management in charge of its operations and available at its office to the public. A common manager may serve two or more Licensees subject to prior written SBA approval; a general or common manager shall be deemed an officer of the Licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management must be qualified and available; using common managers requires SBA approval and they count as officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement — office and public access (§107.101(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee shall maintain a reasonably accessible office displaying the Licensee name, open to the public during regular business hours, and prominently display the license certificate in the principal office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical office presence and public accessibility are required; license certificate must be conspicuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement — diversified investment policy (§107.101(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specifically authorized by SBA in writing, a Licensee shall not maintain more than one-third of its portfolio, as of the close of any full fiscal year, in any small business concern or concerns classified under any single Major Group of the SIC Manual. Prepayments or similar events beyond Licensee's control within the fiscal year shall be disregarded in determining compliance at fiscal year close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforces sector diversification; SBA may grant written exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement — minimum capital (§107.101(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Licensee shall have combined private paid-in capital and paid-in surplus not less than $150,000 and adequate to assure reasonable prospect of sound, profitable, actively and prudently managed operations in accordance with the Act and Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum capitalization and sufficiency for sound operation are required; adequacy is a qualitative standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement — shareholders borrowing to buy stock (§107.101(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Shareholders owning 10% or more of any class of Licensee's stock may not use borrowed funds to purchase such stock unless each such shareholder's net worth is at least twice the amount borrowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents leveraged ownership by significant shareholders unless net worth supports borrowed purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement — time-limit for compliance (§107.101(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing Licensees must comply with the management and office requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) no later than June 30, 1968.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides deadline for bringing existing Licensees into compliance (historical effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: License application requirements (§107.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: License application must be submitted on SBA Form No. 415 in accordance with instructions and accompanied by a $500 license fee paid to SBA upon filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified form and pay fee simultaneously with filing; follow instructions exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of license application (§107.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA shall publish Federal Register notice including name and location of proposed Licensee, area(s) of operations, names/addresses of agent for correspondence and officers/directors/owners of 10%+, and other info SBA deems appropriate, providing opportunity for written comments within a designated period. A similar notice shall be published in a local newspaper and a copy furnished to SBA within 10 days after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and public comment; Licensee must provide required information for notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability of license (§107.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: A license is not transferable in any manner except under circumstances expressly approved in writing by SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers of license or control require prior written SBA approval per §107.701 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of license (§107.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall not surrender its license without prior written SBA approval. Request must be accompanied by immediate payment offer of all debts owing to SBA or a satisfactory plan for fair orderly liquidation of obligations. SBA may remove Licensee from published lists and may examine Licensee; SBA may impose terms/conditions in granting approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrender requires SBA approval and demonstration of satisfactory handling of SBA obligations; SBA retains oversight and may condition approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for SBA purchase of debentures (§107.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for purchase of debentures pursuant to section 303(b) shall be submitted to SBA on SBA Form No. 416 with accompanying instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified application form and follow instructions for borrowing by Licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA funds under §303(b)(2) — venture capital ratio (§107.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for SBA funds under section 303(b)(2), at least 65% of a Licensee's total funds available for investment must be actually invested (or committed) in venture capital financing of small business concerns. Total funds available is defined per Financial Report (SBA Form 468) items. Venture capital investments are valued on the same basis as assets comprising total funds available. Licensee indebted under section 303(b)(2) must maintain this ratio as of March 31 and September 30 each year; SBA may approve temporary lesser ratios in appropriate cases (prepayments, raising private capital, recent loan funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees must track and report venture-capital ratio per specified dates; SBA can grant temporary waivers/adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA sale/assignment of securities evidencing loan (§107.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA may, in its discretion, and upon such terms/conditions and for such consideration as deemed reasonable, sell, assign, transfer or otherwise dispose of any debenture or other evidence of debt or security held in connection with loans made under the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA retains market/credit discretion to transfer its loan assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection or compromise of Licensee indebtedness to SBA (§107.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator or delegate may, in discretion and on reasonable terms and conditions, collect or compromise obligations assigned to or held by SBA and all legal and equitable rights accruing in connection with such obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA has authority to negotiate or settle debts subject to reasonable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum financing term and amortization (§107.301(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All financing of small business concerns by a Licensee shall be for a minimum period of five years (except as otherwise provided), but voluntary prepayment is permitted. Amortization during the first 5 years shall not be required at a rate exceeding an accumulated average of 20% of principal per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets long-term financing expectations and limits initial amortization burden on portfolio concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum interest rate and related charges (§107.301(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum annual cost to a small business concern for average outstanding net funds advanced or guaranteed by the Licensee shall not exceed the lesser of (1) the maximum allowable cost prescribed by applicable State/local law or (2) 15% per annum. Cost includes all interest, discount, fees, commissions, charges (other than charges for management consulting services duly rendered), which are treated as additional discount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All-in cost cap ensures borrower protection; management consulting service charges are excluded from this cap but treated separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20% single-concern investment limitation (§107.301(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Without prior SBA written approval, aggregate obligations and securities acquired and for which commitments or guarantees may be issued by any Licensee for any single small business concern (including affiliates) shall not exceed 20% of Licensee's combined paid-in capital and paid-in surplus. Special transitional rules apply to SBICs licensed prior to Jan 1, 1968, specifying portions of SBA funds to be included in combined capital for 1968–1972. The 20% limitation applies to funds disbursed and commitments issued, not to face amount of securities; write-downs in carrying value do not reduce the amount computed against the limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps exposure to any one concern; transitional schedule reduces counting of SBA funds over time; calculation basis is disbursed/committed funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term financing to protect investment (§107.301(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term advances may be made to a portfolio concern when reasonably necessary to protect Licensee's existing long-term investment, but such advances plus outstanding previous investment shall not exceed the 20% limit. Advances may not be made for normal short-term requirements of the small business concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows remedial short-term support but prevents using short-term loans for routine working capital in a way that increases exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size status declaration requirement (§107.301(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: No financing or management consulting services shall be provided by a Licensee to any business concern unless (1) Licensee and the concern have executed SBA Form 480 (Size Status Declaration), including Licensee’s determination that size standards are met, or (2) SBA has determined the concern is a small business at the request of either party. Licensee must retain completed Form 480 in records available for SBA examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and retain size-status determinations to support eligibility and for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement statement requirement (§107.301(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon each financing, Licensee shall prepare a settlement statement describing amount and purpose of financing, type of security/instrument, interest rate, amount of discount, fees, commissions and charges, and percentage of actual or potential ownership in the concern represented by the Licensee-held financing documents and accompanying rights. Original shall be furnished to the small business concern; receipted copy and the concern's financial statements shall be retained by Licensee for SBA examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency requirement for financed concerns and recordkeeping obligation for Licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination certification (§107.301(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debtor Licensees shall require small business concerns financed by them after Jan 9, 1968 to certify on SBA Form No. 652-D that they will not illegally discriminate in operations, employment, or facilities as set forth in Part 113; such certification must be retained by Licensee for SBA examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires affirmative nondiscrimination commitments from financed concerns and retention of certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity capital defined (§107.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Equity capital’ means funds received by an incorporated small business concern from a Licensee as consideration for issuance of Equity Securities by such concern to the Licensee. ‘Equity Securities’ includes certificates of stock of any class (with/without conversion rights or stock-like privileges) and debt instruments that provide conversion rights to stock or include detachable/undetachable stock purchase warrants/options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what counts as equity for purposes of equity financing rules and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock options/warrants and conversion rights limits (§107.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: The total cost of all shares of stock that may be acquired through exercise of options, warrants, or conversion rights shall not exceed the amount of Equity Capital supplied to the small business concern. Short-term financings to protect interests may incorporate stock acquisition rights similar to original financing. Stock purchase warrants or options issued in connection with Equity Securities shall expire not later than 10 years from issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps potential dilution/acquisition via options to amount of equity provided; sets maximum warrant/option life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinancing and first refusal on new indebtedness (§107.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a Licensee provides Equity Capital, it may require the concern to (a) refinance outstanding indebtedness so Licensee is sole holder of evidence of indebtedness and/or (b) agree not to incur new indebtedness without Licensee's approval, affording Licensee an opportunity to finance such indebtedness; appropriate exceptions for open account or other short-term credit must be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits protective covenants but requires reasonable exceptions for trade/short-term financing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC guarantee of loans (§107.501)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may guarantee to lending institutions up to 90% of (a) a portfolio concern's obligation under any note, debenture, or other evidence of indebtedness or (b) short-term advances to such concern; provided (1) total liability on guarantees shall not exceed Licensee's debt or equity financing of such concern and (2) such financing plus guarantees do not exceed the 20% single-concern limit under §107.301(c). Guarantees may be issued only at request of the portfolio concern or where necessary to protect Licensee's existing investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows guarantees to leverage lending to portfolio concerns but ties guarantees to existing exposure and overall investment limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of options/warrants from affiliate (§107.502)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may, in exchange for financing provided to a portfolio concern, acquire stock purchase warrants or options in an affiliated concern as defined in §121.3-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits certain cross-affiliate acquisitions; affiliate definitions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments — general and fees (§107.503(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee is authorized to enter into commitments to furnish financing to a small business concern. A reasonable commitment fee may be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment fees are permissible if reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments — repayment periods for funds advanced (§107.503(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Licensee enters into a commitment disbursed on request, it may (notwithstanding §107.301(a) maturity provisions) provide that: funds advanced during the first 2 years of the commitment may become due and payable 5 years after the date of the commitment; funds advanced subsequently may be for a period of 3 years from respective disbursement dates. Amortization of each disbursement shall not be required at an annual average rate exceeding principal divided by number of years of applicable repayment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexible repayment scheduling for committed funds and caps amortization pace for each disbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments — stock options/warrants on commitments (§107.503(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where commitment calls for issuance of stock options or warrants, Licensee may acquire such options/warrants up to full amount of funds disbursed and up to 25% of the undisbursed portion of any commitment not attributable to any default on Licensee's part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits equity sweeteners tied to commitments within specified caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Discretionary Portfolio — authorization and size limit (§107.504(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may establish a Special Discretionary Portfolio with maximum outstanding investments not to exceed 20% of Licensee's total adjusted assets as of most recent financial report to SBA. Total adjusted assets means total assets reduced by outstanding indebtedness of Licensee to SBA and other loans having maturities less than 1 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a special sub-portfolio subject to a 20% cap relative to adjusted asset base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Discretionary Portfolio — permitted investments (§107.504(b)(1)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the 20% limit, Licensee may (1) make financing with minimum term of 5 years amortized at rate not exceeding 40% per annum of declining principal (except final year); (2) make short-term financing of portfolio concerns when reasonably necessary as part of sound financing (supplementing §107.301(d)) but sum of short-term and long-term investments in a concern cannot exceed 20% limit; (3) purchase equity securities of a portfolio concern in open market or negotiated transactions when such acquisition is reasonably necessary for sound financing; (4) within 90 days after a lawful offering is first made, purchase newly issued debt or equity securities in a public offering (limited to newly issued securities when offering mixes new and outstanding), relying on underwriter certification as to origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special Discretionary Portfolio relaxes certain constraints (higher amortization, short-term support, secondary market purchases, participation in public offerings) subject to conditions and the 20% cap; reliance on underwriter certifications permitted for origin assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management consulting services — nature (§107.601(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Management consulting services shall consist only of advice regarding financial, management and operating activities of a small business concern and shall not include performance by the Licensee of any such activity. The phrase has same meaning as ‘consulting and advisory services’ in section 308(b) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees may advise but not perform the operational/management functions of portfolio concerns as consulting services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management consulting services — use of independent contractors (§107.601(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Management consulting services may be performed through an independent consultant under contract with the Licensee, whether or not the consultant has similar contracts with other Licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits outsourcing of consulting functions to independent consultants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management consulting services — records and charges (§107.601(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee shall maintain records for SBA examination of time spent and charges made with respect to management consulting services performed for each small business concern financed. Such charges shall not exceed comparable reasonable charges by established professional non-Licensee consultants/firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires contemporaneous time/charge records and caps fees at reasonable market levels to prevent excess charging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wholly owned subsidiary for management consulting — organization limits (§107.602(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee may organize a corporation solely to provide management consulting services subject to §107.601. All stock must be owned and held by the Licensee; parent may not sell/divest stock though may transfer back to subsidiary treasury to retire/cancel; if subsidiary liquidated, charter surrendered. Each officer/director of subsidiary must simultaneously be officer/director of parent. Licensee's financial investment in subsidiary shall not exceed 1% of Licensee's paid-in capital and paid-in surplus; advances/receivables due from subsidiary shall not exceed 1% of paid-in capital and surplus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict structural and financial limits on wholly owned consulting subsidiaries to control exposure and conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wholly owned subsidiary — parent responsibilities (§107.602(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent-Licensee is responsible for compliance by subsidiary with Act and regulations; reports to SBA shall reflect consolidated figures for both corporations; subsidiary shall make separate reports as required by SBA and be subject to examination; failure by subsidiary to report or submit to examination may be acted upon as noncompliance by parent-Licensee, subjecting parent to penalties/sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent bears regulatory and reporting responsibility and can be sanctioned for subsidiary failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services to banks or other investors or lenders (§107.603)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may render services for and receive compensation from banks or other investors or lenders only in connection with financing of, or provision of management consulting services to, a small business concern by the Licensee in participation or cooperation with such bank or other investors or lenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits collaborative service arrangements but ties them to Licensee’s financing or consulting activities for a small business concern to avoid unrelated third-party fee activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in ownership or control of Licensee — prior SBA approval required (§107.701)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of control of a Licensee by any means is subject to prior written SBA approval. Prior written approval shall be required for: (1) proposed transfer of 10% or more of capital stock; (2) proposed transfer resulting in acquisition of beneficial ownership by any person/affiliated group of 10% or more of capital stock; (3) any proposed change in beneficial ownership that involves or results in a change in control. Unless prior written approval is obtained, no such transaction shall be consummated and neither Licensee nor persons acting on its behalf shall register transfer on books or permit proposed new owner(s) to exercise voting rights or participate in conduct of Licensee’s affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict control-transfer regime to preserve regulatory oversight; 10% thresholds trigger prior-approval obligations and suspension of transfer actions until approval.
